rated_messages.input_message: Pause. Notice what triggered you to smoke in the past. Now take one deep breath and remind yourself that you do not need to smoke.
Pause. Notice what triggered you to smoke in the past. Now take one deep breath and remind yourself that you do not need to smoke.
This craving is just an event. A game. It will pass. The game gets easier the more you let your urge pass without smoking. But, it gets harder every time you give in to the urge and smoke.
Instead of smoking, take 10 deep, slow breaths and count them. Pay attention to what your breathing feels like. If you lose count, that's okay, just start over at 1 until you get to 10.
Some people find that having a simple mantra can really help, especially if things feel stressful. Try repeating something simple to yourself like: "I can do it!".
When you begin to crave a cig, concentrate on your reasons for not smoking. Keep a list on your phone and look at it when you feel yourself beginning to falter.

The best way to deal with any urges from being around smokers is to get out of the situation briefly until it goes. Make an excuse, go to the toilet, go get some water, pretend you need to get some phone reception!

Think of urges as loud construction noises. Sometimes there's nothing you can do except agree that it's annoying. If you fight it, you feel more irritated, right? Let your urge be there until it passes on its own.
Take a deep breath and let it out slowly. Notice that you are completely OK for this one breath. Do it again.

Think about your hero, or someone you admire. What do you admire about them? Often our heroes are people who struggle and succeed in difficult circumstances. Now's the chance to be your own hero - by not smoking despite the challenges of stress and strong urges!
Keep picturing yourself getting home later today knowing that you've gained a smoke-free day. It's nearly a reality!
